topic: The 'drink water to flush toxins' myth

slides.headline: Does massage really release toxins?
slides.sub: Why you're told to drink water, and what's actually true.

slides.title: The myth
slides.body: A popular idea says massage squeezes toxins out of your muscles, so you need to drink water to flush them away. It's a nice story, but research doesn't back it up.

slides.title: What's actually true
slides.body: Your liver and kidneys handle waste around the clock. Massage doesn't load your body with toxins, and extra water won't wash away anything massage stirred up.

slides.title: Why you might feel off after
slides.body: Some tenderness, tiredness or feeling a bit light-headed after a firm massage is common. It usually passes within a day or two and isn't a sign of toxins leaving.

slides.title: Water is still a good idea
slides.body: Having a glass of water after a massage is perfectly fine. It's just ordinary hydration, the same as any other day. Drink to thirst rather than trying to flush anything out.

slides.title: What massage can do
slides.body: Remedial massage can ease muscle tension, help you feel less tight and make it easier to move. It works well alongside exercise and an active plan for any niggle.

slides.headline: Honest massage, no myths
slides.body: Our remedial massage therapists explain what they're doing and why, and set realistic expectations. Book online via the link in bio.

caption:
'Drink lots of water to flush out the toxins.' You've probably heard it after a massage.

It's a popular idea, but research doesn't support it. Massage doesn't release a wave of toxins, and your liver and kidneys handle waste around the clock. Feeling a bit tender or tired afterwards is common and usually passes within a day or two.

A glass of water is still fine, it's just normal hydration. What remedial massage can genuinely do is ease muscle tension and help you move more comfortably, especially alongside exercise.
